title: Coast Live Oak: Old Californian Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: An evergreen oak of coastal California. Glen Ellen's Jack's Oak is about 400 years old, and Los Angeles has two over 200 years old.
intro: Quercus agrifolia keeps its leaves all year and grows along the California coast. Jack's Oak in Glen Ellen, about 400 years old, was scheduled for felling in 2013 until lab tests showed it could stand longer. In Los Angeles the Arboretum's oak is put at over 200 years, older than the city around it, and the Huntington's Chinese Garden grew up around another of 200 to 300 years. Oakland planted its Jack London Oak in front of City Hall in 1917, moved as a young tree of about twenty from Mosswood Park.
